newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: No end in sight yet for Zaire talks in S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: No end in sight yet for Zaire talks in S.Africa.

text.p: Zairean peace talks in South Africa went on through the day on Monday after news broke of a rebel advance to within 30 km (20 miles) of the crucial mining centre and second largest city of Lubumbashi.

Rebel forces vowing to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko closed in on the city while political clashes rocked the capital, Kinshasa, but there was no comment from the rivals meeting for peace talks at a secret location.
A Pretoria Foreign Ministry spokesman said full delegations representing the Mobutu government and rebel leader Laurent Kabila began meeting shortly after 10 a.m. (0800 GMT).

"What's been happening is the Deputy President Thabo Mbeki and other (South African) representatives spent all day conferring with the leadership of both parties, separately and jointly," he told Reuters.
"Yesterday the talks were more structured. Today it was more conferring."
It was not clear if the talks would end on Monday evening or continue into Tuesday, he said.
The spokesman declined to say what progress had been made or when the participants might be ready to make a statement.

The negotiators moved to a secret location near Pretoria after a frosty start on Saturday when rebel envoy Bizima Karaha in effect told the Kinshasa government delegation it was now or never if they wanted a peaceful settlement.
The talks are being brokered jointly by South Africa and the United Nations, which is being represented by the joint U.N. and Organisation of African Unity envoy Mohamed Sahnoun.
